gloss: getting caught up in; being involved; collateral damage

definitions.gloss: getting caught up in; being involved in (something negative)
definitions.explanation: Being drawn into a troublesome situation, conflict, or accident without originally being a party to it. Often implies innocent involvement in someone else's problem.

examples.japanese: {喧嘩|けんか}の{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えを{食|く}った。
examples.english: I got caught up in their fight.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}で{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えになった{通行人|つうこうにん}がいた。
examples.english: There were passersby who got caught up in the accident.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えにならないよう、{距離|きょり}を{置|お}いている。
examples.english: I'm keeping my distance so I don't get involved.

notes:
COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{巻|ま}き (winding, wrapping - from {巻|ま}く) + {添|ぞ}え (accompanying - from {添|そ}える)

The image is of being "wound up" or "wrapped into" something.

KEY EXPRESSIONS:
・{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えを{食|く}う - to get caught up in (passive involvement)
・{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えになる - to become involved
・{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えにする - to drag someone into
・{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}えを{避|さ}ける - to avoid getting involved

NUANCE:
Always negative - implies:
- Unwilling involvement
- Innocent third party affected
- Unfortunate circumstance
- Collateral damage

COMMON CONTEXTS:
・{事故|じこ}の{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught in an accident
・{争|あらそ}いの{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught in a dispute
・{犯罪|はんざい}の{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - implicated in a crime
・{リストラ|りすとら}の{巻|ま}き{添|ぞ}え - caught up in layoffs

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・とばっちり - splash damage, undeserved consequence
・{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる - to be drawn into
・{飛|と}び{火|び} - spreading (of trouble)
・{累|るい}が{及|およ}ぶ - to suffer consequences (formal)

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in everyday conversation and news reports.
